correctness.rationale: For every link and N>=2, vanishing adjacent hub amplitudes implies all Taylor moments vanish; H^2= w†v and H^3=(h_j+h_{j+1})w†v+w†D_jv. Nonzero two-edge path product forces u_j=ell_j. If w†v=0 and D_j=epsilon_j I, normalized v,w are orthonormal arm modes, each attaches to only one adjacent hub; N 2/3-dimensional invariant blocks form a complete orthonormal basis. Matrix-exponential direct sum proves all-time cage property. Nonzero m2 or m3 yields the sharp t²/t³ interhub transfer-amplitude orders and t⁴/t⁶ transition-probability orders. The packaged checker independently reconstructs random nonuniform matrices, tests the full block diagonalization and its spectrum, time propagator and failure perturbations: 2970 passed assertions, max error 2.52e-14.

originality.rationale: The original AB effect, finite cages, local unitary detangling, and especially equal-arm-potential disorder at fixed homogeneous hoppings are explicitly prior art (Vidal 1998; Flach 2014; Ahmed 2022/23). The examined full texts and returned meaning-based published-finding corpus records did not identify or imply the joint exact iff for arbitrary diamond-by-diamond nonzero complex bond amplitudes subject to the necessary local product-balance condition, with arbitrary hub and common arm energies, together with all-site cage block decomposition and two distinct leakage onset orders. General local-unitary constructions could still subsume the statement; historical priority remains provisional.
residual_risks: The 2014 general local-unitary detangling/generator framework may imply an equivalent block decomposition after specialization; the inspected text does not decisively settle historical priority.
Post-2016 symmetric-potential diamond-chain studies already contain exact all-time caging as a strict special case; no novelty is claimed for that subcase.
The necessary/sufficient classification is confined to open two-arm-per-link graph topology with every four-edge hopping nonzero.

value.rationale: Exact confinement under arbitrarily strong, independently varying hopping disorder is the physically motivated design question. The non-periodic complete iff criterion and explicit finite-cage decomposition identify a robust correlated-disorder manifold, while distinct transfer-amplitude orders t² and t³ (and probabilities t⁴ and t⁶) distinguish destructive-interference and onsite-symmetry failures. The answer is a complete natural classification rather than an arbitrary parameter slice or simple known table lookup.
